summary.text: 后 is attested as a graph for a ruler and for a ruler’s principal wife. In simplified Chinese, it also writes the separate word “after/behind,” for which traditional Chinese uses 後; this spelling loan is associated with similar pronunciation, though an ancient sound match is not established here.

formation.text: The graph’s formation is disputed. An early lexicographic analysis describes a human figure issuing commands and relates the graph to 一 and 口. Other accounts connect early forms with 司 or 毓. These interpretations do not establish a secure decomposition of the received graph.

components.text: 口 is visible in the received graph and appears in an early lexicographic analysis. That account does not establish an independent meaning or role for it in the graph’s origin.

history.text: Accounts of the early graph differ: one treats 后 and 司 as the same graph, with their orientations distinguished in bronze forms; another reports an oracle form written with 毓. These accounts do not establish a sequence leading to the received form.
The received form contains 口, but the early lexicographic analysis does not explain how this visible form arose.

uncertainties.text: The graph’s early origin remains disputed. Childbirth and rear-body interpretations have been proposed, but neither a depiction nor a secure component analysis is established here.
Classical use of 后 for 後 and their modern consolidation are reported, but their chronology remains unresolved in the available accounts.

senses.period: Late Spring and Autumn bronze inscriptions; primary examples not independently verified
senses.text: A late Spring and Autumn bronze use is reported with the meaning “ruler.” Any earlier oracle use of the same graph and word is not securely dated here.

senses.period: Received textual usage; transition date unresolved
senses.text: Received-text examples document 后 for a ruler’s principal wife. They do not establish when, or whether, this sense developed from “ruler.”

senses.period: Classical spelling use reported; precise chronology unresolved; current in simplified Chinese
senses.text: In simplified Chinese, 后 writes the separate word “after/behind,” represented by 後 in traditional Chinese. This is a spelling loan, not a documented change in the meaning of 后. Both graphs are pronounced hòu in modern Mandarin, but an ancient sound match is not established here.

developments.text: Both senses are documented, but their relationship and any development between them are unresolved.

The graph 后 was reused to write the distinct word written 後 because the words were reported to sound alike or similarly. They share the modern Mandarin reading hòu, but an ancient sound match and the loan’s precise chronology are unresolved.

limitations.text: The available attestations do not establish a dated semantic chain from childbirth or succession to “ruler” or “empress.”

overview.text: 后 is attested for a ruler and a ruler’s principal wife. In simplified Chinese it also writes “after/behind”: the separate graph 後 was borrowed because the words were reported to sound alike, though an ancient sound match is unconfirmed.

components.text: 口 appears in the received graph and in an early analysis, but its original role in 后 is unsettled.
